Maria Chen: Thanks everyone for the workshop — dropping the summary and decisions here so we have a single source of truth.

Aj Patel: Quick recap of customer asks we surfaced: Acme wants predictable cost controls for high-throughput chat; Nimbla asked for quantization recommendations for embeddings; Atlas asked for eval-triggered alerts tied to prompt sets.

David Li: Proposed scope for the Optimize toolkit MVP (discussed):
- batching: per-route config + econ-aware suggestion engine
- caching: prefix/KV caching as a first-class policy
- quantization: recommender that outputs suggested profiles (no auto-apply)
- eval alerts: webhook + severity tags for ops

Sophia Ramos: Suggest we split work into Alpha vs Beta:
- Alpha (safe): recommendations + basic batching knobs + non-destructive caching (read-only cache hints)
- Beta: autoscale batching policies, cache write path, and quant apply pipeline (with rollback)

Maria Chen: Launch criteria we agreed on for Alpha:
- Performance: P95 latency regression <= +10% on targeted routes under pilot load
- Economic: >= 15% token-cost reduction on batched/rec workloads for pilot tenants
- Quality: eval-alert false-positive rate <= 5% on seed prompt sets
- Security/compliance: per-tenant isolation for caches + audit logs enabled

Eli Green: Pilot customers: Acme (chat-heavy), Nimbla (embed-heavy), and 1 internal product team. Timeline target: 8 weeks to Alpha pilot, 12 weeks for Beta readiness.

Aj Patel: Tradeoffs we flagged: aggressive batching gives ~25–35% unit cost reduction but can add 10–30ms tail latency depending on seq-length variance. Recommendation: make batching QoS-configurable per route + provide econ score so customers can choose.

David Li: Technical notes: runtime already supports continuous batching and KV cache hooks. For quantization, we'll surface model-family templates (e.g., Llama2/7b -> int8/static) and per-workload sim tests. Recommender will output: profile name, expected mem/cost delta, expected quality risk (low/med/high).

Sophia Ramos: Customer-driven asks to capture in scope: per-tenant guardrails (don't recommend >20% perf-risk without approval), explainability string for each recommendation, and an opt-in eval-triggered alert path that can call customer webhook or create a Redwood support ticket.

Maria Chen: Decision (MVP / Alpha): include per-route batching knobs (min/max batch, latency cap), cold-start prefix caching (read-then-promote), quantization recommender (suggest-only), and eval-alert webhook with severity + simple suppression rules.

Eli Green: Acceptance tests for Alpha pilot: run 1M requests/day synthetic with production-like seq-length distribution, verify P95 regression <=+12% (allowing small leeway in CI), verify econ delta reported per-route and per-tenant, and validate alerting plumbing with 3 sample evals.

Aj Patel: Action items — owners:
- David Li: recommender prototype + design doc (2w)
- Eli Green: pilot harness + perf test configs (1w)
- Sophia Ramos: customer onboarding checklist, acceptance criteria doc, and pilot comms (1w)
- Maria Chen: coordinate pilot contracts and SLAs

David Li: I'll open the design PR tomorrow and paste link here: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/optimize-recommender (draft).
